name: Chenru Hou
affiliation: Humboldt-Universität zu Berlin · BGSS | Friedrich-Alexander-Universität Erlangen-Nürnberg
intro: I study educational inequality, classroom diversity, and social networks among students. My research examines how peer relationships connect classroom contexts with student outcomes and educational opportunities.
about: I am a doctoral researcher in the sociology of education at Humboldt-Universität zu Berlin and a member of the Berlin Graduate School of Social Sciences (BGSS). My dissertation investigates how multidimensional classroom diversity relates to student outcomes and educational inequality through peer relationships. My research also examines governance structures and networks within Germany’s Startchancen programme.

experience.title: Research Associate · MuHiK
experience.institution: IQB (Dec 2021 – Apr 2023); University of Potsdam (Apr 2023 – Dec 2025)
experience.detail: Worked on the BMBF-funded project on multidimensional classroom heterogeneity: measurement, effects, and mechanisms. Responsibilities included data analysis, coordination of two meta-analyses, supervision of student assistants, visualisation, project reporting, and research communication.

methods: Social network analysis (SAOM, ERGM), multilevel modelling, longitudinal analysis, structural equation modelling, and causal inference. I use R and RStudio for reproducible analysis, data management, and visualisation, with experience working with IQB-Bildungstrend, NEPS, and ESS data.

teaching.title: Researching educational inequality with large-scale data
teaching.detail: A methods-focused course combining empirical research and practical data analysis. Topics included educational inequality, large-scale data, regression and multilevel analysis, causal inference, and cross-national comparisons.
